base: The component slot holds only a pointer: the add-helper bg3.exe+0x1DD0050 allocates a 0x68-byte object (FUN_1441BEB10(..., 0x68)), constructs it with bg3.exe+0x2058380 and stores the pointer through ComponentFrameStorageAllocRaw(storage, 8); the registry size 112 = object 0x68 + 8, as with the other objects stored behind a pointer. The fields below are that object; the last 8 bytes are outside it.

fields.name: Values
fields.evidence: ls::PrimitiveQueue<ecl::sound::AutoFoleyDataComponent::WindowValue> (macOS template names) ring buffer. Constructor bg3.exe+0x2058380 allocates it with FUN_141DCFA10(capacity) when the capacity is non-zero, then pushes capacity default elements of 0x28 bytes (FUN_141DCEB30: vec3 0, quat 0,0,0,1, double time 0 at +0x20).

fields.name: Capacity
fields.evidence: Constructor stores the capacity argument here (live: always 2).

fields.name: Count
fields.evidence: Constructor zeroes it before the pushes (live: 2).

fields.name: TransformWindow
fields.evidence: Constructor bg3.exe+0x2058380 builds the queue at +0 with the first capacity argument; the per-entity job of AutoFoleySystem (Toolkit FUN_180EBDD70) pushes {translation, rotation, game time} of the skeleton sound object into it.

fields.name: VelocityWindow
fields.evidence: Constructor builds the queue at +0x18 (pointer +0x18, capacity +0x20, count +0x24, head -1 at +0x28, tail +0x2C) with the second capacity argument; the job pushes the per-second deltas of the first queue.

fields.name: Velocity
fields.evidence: Constructor zeroes +0x30..+0x3B; reader bg3.exe+0x1DCB410 takes the length of the three floats +0x30/+0x34/+0x38 as a maximum speed.

fields.name: AngularVelocity
fields.evidence: Constructor writes 0,0,0 and 1.0 at +0x48 (identity, w last); reader bg3.exe+0x1DCB410 takes the length of the four floats +0x3C..+0x48.

fields.name: Acceleration
fields.evidence: Constructor zeroes +0x4C..+0x57; reader takes the length of +0x4C/+0x50/+0x54.

fields.name: AngularAcceleration
fields.evidence: Constructor writes 0,0,0 and 1.0 at +0x64; reader takes the length of the four floats +0x58..+0x64. The object ends at +0x68. Live values here include very small (denormal) floats, which the raw check rejects although they are ordinary deltas of a quaternion.

fields.name: _Pad68
fields.evidence: Outside the 0x68-byte object (registry size = object + 8); live bytes there are whatever follows the allocation (heap pointers, a null entity handle).

open_questions: Names of the vector members are ours; whether the deltas are per second or per frame is not re-checked on Windows (the Windows per-entity job was not located; the Toolkit's FUN_180EBDD70 was the source).
The raw check on this type rejects denormal floats in AngularAcceleration; the type is still float (reader bg3.exe+0x1DCB410 squares and sums them).
second_pass: Windows add-helper bg3.exe+0x1DD0050 shows the slot is a pointer to a 0x68-byte object; its constructor bg3.exe+0x2058380 sets every member (two 24-byte queues, zeros, identity quaternions with 1.0 at +0x48 and +0x64) and the reader bg3.exe+0x1DCB410 reads the four vectors at +0x30/+0x3C/+0x4C/+0x58; the old field_68/field_6C were bytes past the object.
